- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.22) within 5 days, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 5-day average is below 70.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-term decline; if true outcome drops below 65 after 20+ days, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., -0.61, -0.22, 0.11), model tends to overcorrect; apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias for next 3–5 days.
